hook.convey: short lengths add up: many 100 m races (or about 20 m cricket pitches) end to end → a long distance; that long distance gets its own big unit, the kilometre; 1 km = 1000 m, and below the metre sits the cm, 1 m = 100 cm

use.hi: Cricket pitch lagbhag 20 m lamba hota hai. Aise 50 pitch ek line mein rakho, toh 50 × 20 = 1000 m ho jaate hain. Itni lambi doori ka apna ek bada unit hai: kilometre.
use.en: A cricket pitch is about 20 m long. Put 50 such pitches in a line and 50 × 20 = 1000 m. A distance that long has its own big unit: the kilometre.

use.hi: School bus ghar se school tak kai km chalti hai. Aaj dekhenge ki 1 km mein kitne metre hote hain, aur 1 metre mein kitne cm.
use.en: The school bus goes several km from home to school. Today we see how many metres are in 1 km, and how many cm are in 1 metre.

explain.convey: 100 m sports-day race laid end to end again and again → at 1000 m the kilometre is complete → 1 km = 1000 m, not 100 m

point.hi: Sports day ki 100 m ki daud socho. Aisi daud ek ke baad ek jodte jao. Jab kul 1000 m ho jaate hain, tab 1 km poora hota hai. Toh 1 km = 1000 m, sirf 100 m nahi.
point.en: Think of the 100 m race on sports day. Join such races one after another. When the total reaches 1000 m, 1 km is complete. So 1 km = 1000 m, not just 100 m.

prompt.hi: 1 km poora karne ke liye 100 m wali kitni daud ek ke baad ek lagani padengi?
prompt.en: How many 100 m races, one after another, are needed to complete 1 km?

why.hi: ek daud 100 m ki hai, aur 10 × 100 m = 1000 m, jo 1 km hai
why.en: one race is 100 m, and 10 × 100 m = 1000 m, which is 1 km

simpler.hi: 100 m ki daud ek ke baad ek jodte jao. Jab kul 1000 m ho jaayein, tab 1 km poora hota hai.
simpler.en: Keep joining 100 m races one after another. When the total is 1000 m, 1 km is complete.

explain.convey: two separate facts, never mixed: 1 km = 1000 m (big to middle) and 1 m = 100 cm (middle to small); km biggest, then m, then cm

point.hi: Do alag jodiyan yaad rakho: 1 km = 1000 m, aur 1 m = 100 cm. Sabse bada unit km hai, phir m, aur sabse chhota cm. Metre ke andar 100 cm aate hain, 1000 nahi. Yeh rekha metre mein bani hai.
point.en: Remember two separate pairs: 1 km = 1000 m, and 1 m = 100 cm. The biggest unit is km, then m, and the smallest is cm. A metre holds 100 cm, not 1000. This line is marked in metres.

prompt.hi: Ek kapde ka tukda 2 m lamba hai. Woh kitne cm lamba hai?
prompt.en: A piece of cloth is 2 m long. How many cm long is it?

why.hi: har m mein 100 cm hain, aur 2 × 100 = 200
why.en: each m holds 100 cm, and 2 × 100 = 200

simpler.hi: km aur m ki jodi mein 1000 hai, par m aur cm ki jodi mein 100. Ek metre mein 100 cm hote hain.
simpler.en: The km and m pair uses 1000, but the m and cm pair uses 100. One metre holds 100 cm.

explain.convey: the same distance in two units: 3 km = 3000 m → the bigger unit gives the smaller number, the smaller unit the bigger number, because one km holds 1000 m

point.hi: Ek hi doori ko dekho: 3 km = 3000 m. km mein likho toh chhota number aata hai, metre mein likho toh bada number. Bada unit, chhota number, kyunki ek km mein 1000 m samaate hain. Yeh rekha metre mein hai.
point.en: Look at one distance: 3 km = 3000 m. Written in km it is a smaller number, written in metres a bigger number. Bigger unit, smaller number, because one km holds 1000 m. This line is in metres.

prompt.hi: Ek sadak 8000 m lambi hai. Yeh sadak kitne km lambi hai?
prompt.en: A road is 8000 m long. How many km long is this road?

why.hi: har 1000 m ka 1 km banta hai, aur 8000 m mein 8 baar 1000 m hai

simpler.hi: 3 km aur 3000 m ek hi doori hai. km bada unit hai, isliye usmein number chhota aata hai.
simpler.en: 3 km and 3000 m are one and the same distance. km is the bigger unit, so its number comes out smaller.
